the Lite definer RPCs (can_lead_session, promote_highlight, create_workspace, transfer_leadership) and the broadcast triggers

scope: Two additive migrations (grants and one profiles policy) and their checks in the live RLS suite. Out of scope: any schema/column change, the function bodies, and the seed.

acceptance_criteria.text: Anon is denied on create_workspace; authenticated is allowed, and the policy helpers stay callable (the suite proves it).
A teammate reads a co-member's profile; an outsider does not; the owner's own-profile policy is untouched.
rls.sql gains the g17/g18 checks in the existing harness style.
README §6 and the task review mark the two items done.

open_questions: The changes are additive: no column or function body changes, so 02 §8.1 (the schema's source of truth) does not move.

Supabase grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default; the fix revokes from PUBLIC and anon and grants authenticated, plus the default privileges for later functions. This is the mechanism DB-Q/DB-1 imply, not a new decision.
The live RLS suite is the gate; it needs Docker and the local stack, so its run is recorded as the task's test and deferred in this environment.
risks: Revoking EXECUTE from PUBLIC removes it from authenticated too; the explicit grant restores it, and the suite verifies the policy helpers still work.
A profiles policy that checked membership naively could leak other teams; the policy joins on a shared team_members row.
The default-privileges statements only affect future functions; existing ones are covered by the revoke/grant above.
